limitations: Not a hostile-directory sandbox; no atomic dirfd containment/conditional target-kind replacement.
No arbitrary/network/removable filesystem certificate; explicit controlled-local profile required.
Linux/Node24 local execution not claimed; subsequent CI can verify the candidate branches.
No crash/power-loss/restart recovery or remote publisher fencing protocol.
Unknown native outcomes without an authoritative witness remain unresolved; no automatic republish/rollback.
Journal and committed version files are intentionally retained; separate copy costs roughly one extra output file.
No new browser/AAC/Opus matrix, RSS/GC benchmark or P27/P28 public integration run.
No commit/push/new CI/tag/release/npm publication in this stage.
